content: Mifepristone affects the metabolism of various drugs by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, leading to increased levels or effects of these drugs. This interaction necessitates careful consideration of alternative therapies or dose adjustments to avoid adverse effects. Below are the detailed interactions and recommendations for specific drugs: 1. Ranolazine: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of ranolazine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 2. Regorafenib: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of regorafenib via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or consider an alternative therapy. 3. Repotrectinib: Mifepristone elevates the levels or effects of repotrectinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Discontinue strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors and wait 3-5 elimination half-lives before initiating repotrectinib. 4. Ribociclib: Both mifepristone and ribociclib prolong the QTc interval. Mifepristone increases ribociclib levels or effects via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 5. Rifabutin: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of rifabutin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 6. Rimegepant: Mifepristone elevates the levels or effects of rimegepant through CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 7. Riociguat: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of riociguat by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor for signs of hypotension and adjust the dose if necessary. 8. Romidepsin: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of romidepsin via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 9. Rosuvastatin: Mifepristone increases the toxicity of rosuvastatin through mechanisms other than CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 10. Selumetinib: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of selumetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the selumetinib dosage as per its monograph. After discontinuing the inhibitor, resume the original selumetinib dose after 3 elimination half-lives. 11. Sevoflurane: Both mifepristone and sevoflurane prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 12. Sildenafil: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of sildenafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 13. Siponimod: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of siponimod via CYP3A4 inhibition. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 14. Sonidegib: Mifepristone elevates the levels or effects of sonidegib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 15. Sparsentan: Mifepristone and sparsentan increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, interrupt sparsentan treatment and consider dose titration upon resumption. 16. Stiripentol: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of stiripentol via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 17. Suvorexant: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of suvorexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 18. Tazemetostat: Mifepristone elevates the levels or effects of tazemetostat through CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid tazemetostat coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 19. Tetrabenazine: Both mifepristone and tetrabenazine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 20. Tezacaftor: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of tezacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 21. Tiagabine: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of tiagabine via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 22. Tipranavir: Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of mifepristone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 23. Tolterodine: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of tolterodine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is necessary during chronic mifepristone therapy, reduce the tolterodine IR dose to 1 mg twice daily and the ER dose to 2 mg once daily. Monitor for QT prolongation. 24. Tolvaptan: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of tolvaptan via CYP3A4 inhibition. This combination is contraindicated. 25. Toremifene: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of toremifene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 26. Tovorafenib: Mifepristone elevates the levels or effects of tovorafenib by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid tovorafenib coadministration with strong or moderate CYP2C8 inhibitors. 27. Trabectedin: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of trabectedin via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 28. Trazodone: Mifepristone elevates the levels or effects of trazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 29. Triptorelin: Triptorelin increases mifepristone toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval, raising the risk of torsades de pointes. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 30. Tucatinib: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of tucatinib through other mechanisms. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the dose of CYP3A substrates as per product labeling. 31. Ubrogepant: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of ubrogepant via CYP3A4 inhibition. This combination is contraindicated. 32. Ulipristal: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of ulipristal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 33. Umeclidinium bromide/Vilanterol inhaled: Mifepristone increases the toxicity of this combination by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Exercise caution when coadministering vilanterol with drugs that prolong the QTc interval. 34. Valbenazine: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of valbenazine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 35. Vandetanib: Mifepristone elevates the levels or effects of vandetanib via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 36. Vemurafenib: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of vemurafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 37. Venetoclax: Mifepristone elevates the levels or effects of venetoclax through CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 38. Vilanterol/Fluticasone furoate inhaled: Mifepristone increases the toxicity of this combination by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 39. Voriconazole: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of voriconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 40. Abemaciclib: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of abemaciclib via CYP3A4 inhibition. Modify therapy and monitor closely. If dose reduction to 100 mg twice daily is required due to adverse reactions, further reduce to 50 mg twice daily if necessary. Discontinue abemaciclib if the patient cannot tolerate 50 mg twice daily. If mifepristone is discontinued, increase the abemaciclib dose to the original level after 3-5 half-lives of mifepristone. 41. Acalabrutinib: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of acalabrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Limit the acalabrutinib dose to 100 mg once daily and monitor for drug-related toxicity. 42. Ado-trastuzumab emtansine: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of ado-trastuzumab emtansine via CYP3A4 inhibition. Modify therapy and monitor closely for adverse reactions. 43. Albuterol: Both mifepristone and albuterol prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Alprazolam: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of alprazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Amiodarone: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of amiodarone through other mechanisms, including CYP2C8/2C9 inhibition. Use the smallest recommended doses for substrates and monitor closely. Avoid coadministration if alternatives are available. 46. Amitriptyline: Both mifepristone and amitriptyline prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 47. Amlodipine: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of amlodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Amobarbital: Amobarbital decreases the levels or effects of mifepristone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Amoxapine: Both mifepristone and amoxapine prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 50. Apixaban: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of apixaban by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Avoid coadministration. 51. Apomorphine: Both mifepristone and apomorphine prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 52. Aprepitant: Aprepitant increases the levels or effects of mifepristone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Arformoterol: Both mifepristone and arformoterol prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 54. Aripiprazole: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of aripiprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Follow manufacturer recommendations if coadministration is necessary. 55. Arsenic trioxide: Both mifepristone and arsenic trioxide prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 56. Artemether: Both mifepristone and artemether prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 57. Artemether/Lumefantrine: Both mifepristone and this combination prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 58. Asenapine: Both mifepristone and asenapine prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 59. Atazanavir: Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of mifepristone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Do not exceed 300 mg/day of mifepristone for Cushing syndrome when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely for toxicity. 60. Atogepant: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of atogepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. The recommended atogepant dosage is 10 mg once daily when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 61. Atomoxetine: Both mifepristone and atomoxetine prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 62. Atorvastatin: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of atorvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. The atorvastatin dose should not exceed 40 mg/day when administered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 63. Avatrombopag: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of avatrombopag by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the starting dose of avatrombopag to 20 mg three times weekly when treating ITP. Monitor platelet counts and adjust the dose as necessary. 64. Axitinib: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of axitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 65. Azithromycin: Both mifepristone and azithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 66. Bedaquiline: Both mifepristone and bedaquiline prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Avoid concurrent use of bedaquiline for more than 14 days unless benefits justify the risks. 67. Boceprevir: Boceprevir increases the levels or effects of mifepristone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Do not exceed 300 mg/day of mifepristone for Cushing syndrome when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 68. Bortezomib: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of bortezomib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 69. Bosentan: Bosentan decreases the levels or effects of mifepristone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Coadministration is not recommended by the manufacturer. 70. Brentuximab vedotin: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of brentuximab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 71. Brexpiprazole: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of brexpiprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 72. Brigatinib: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of brigatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the brigatinib dose by approximately 50% if coadministration is necessary. Resume the original dose after discontinuing mifepristone. 73. Bupropion: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of bupropion by inhibiting CYP2B6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 74. Buspirone: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of buspirone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Start with 5 mg twice daily and adjust the dose based on clinical response. 75. Cabozantinib: Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of cabozantinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the cabozantinib dose if coadministration is necessary. For patients taking cabozantinib tablets, reduce the dose by 20 mg (e.g., from 60 mg/day to 40 mg/day).
